notes: Motor wires and battery-holder leads are pre-attached (motors soldered if needed), so they are modelled as the motor/holder ports going directly into the controller's screw terminals; no separate jumper wires.

The motor controller board is a new part type; it is a HAT pushed onto the first 26 GPIO pins. Only the pins used by the gpiozero Robot (GPIO7, 8, 9, 10) plus one GND are modelled; the exact GND pin (GND.1) is an assumption.
Terminal labels A/B (motors) and +/- (battery) follow the manual; the board's own labels may differ.
Motor polarity is arbitrary (swap pins in code to fix direction).
Chassis, wheels, ball caster, USB power bank for the Pi and optional components (breadboard, distance/line sensors) are not part of the electrical build and are omitted.
The left/right assignment of motor1/motor2 is arbitrary; the manual has the user test and swap pin numbers in code.
